claim: Calling IsValid() inside CommandResponseFromJSON makes the shared deserializer (also used by Client4.ExecuteCommand/ExecuteCommandWithTeam to parse the server's own API response) reject responses the server itself emits, since api4/command.go encodes the CommandResponse with no write-path validation and plugin ExecuteCommand hooks / CreateCommandPost accept any ResponseType; a plugin returning an unlisted ResponseType yields HTTP 200 from the server but a decode failure in the Go SDK — the type cannot round-trip its own output.

claim: The hardcoded local `maxLength := 65535` duplicates the exported constant PostMessageMaxBytesV2, counts bytes via len() where every sibling validator counts runes against PostMessageMaxRunesV2 (16383), and imposes a fixed ceiling upstream of the store's configurable post-size limit derived from the DB column with no admin override; ephemeral responses (never length-checked before, since SendEphemeralPost skips Post.IsValid) are now capped too. Validator dissented toward Medium.

claim: IsValid() recurses into ExtraResponses and propagates any nested failure, so one invalid nested extra_responses entry makes CommandResponseFromJSON return nil for the whole payload — the valid main message is discarded and the caller gets a 500 (app/command.go:597) or 400 (web/webhook.go:113-116) with no post; this contradicts HandleCommandResponse's deliberate per-entry tolerance, and the error does not identify which nested entry failed. The new test at command_response_test.go:171-182 encodes this all-or-nothing behavior.
raw: #3 🟡 Medium: One invalid nested `extra_responses` entry discards the entire response, including the valid main message
